title: Database Connection Pool Exhaustion
snippet: Connection pool exhaustion occurs when active connections reach the configured maximum, typically caused by traffic spikes, slow queries holding connections open, or a connection leak. Short-term mitigation is restarting the affected service to release stale connections; the durable fix is increasing pool size or resolving the underlying slow queries.

title: JWT Signing Key Rotation Procedure
snippet: Token validation failures with a signature mismatch usually indicate the token was signed with a key no longer recognized as active, often following an incomplete key rotation. Resolution requires rotating the signing key and ensuring all instances load the updated key set.

title: Diagnosing Slow Database Queries
snippet: Elevated response times with normal CPU and memory usage often point to database-side query degradation rather than application load. Common causes include missing indexes, query plan regressions, or lock contention. Diagnosis should compare query latency against historical baselines before restarting application services.

title: Identity Provider Outage Runbook
snippet: When login failures rise but the identity provider reports normal latency and health, the issue is more likely local configuration (signing keys, token audience/issuer mismatch) than an IdP-side outage. Verify IdP health metrics before escalating to the identity provider vendor.

title: Service Restart Best Practices
snippet: Restarting a service clears in-memory state, connection handles, and stuck threads, which resolves transient issues like connection leaks or memory bloat. It does not resolve issues rooted in external dependencies, configuration, or database-side degradation, and should be treated as a low-risk first attempt rather than a guaranteed fix.

title: Scaling Database Connection Capacity
snippet: When restarts fail to resolve connection pool exhaustion, increasing the connection pool size or scaling the underlying database resolves sustained high-traffic exhaustion. This action is considered higher risk as it changes resource allocation and should be approved before execution in production environments.
